added_lemmas.gap: The exact-uniform construction does not establish achievability under an unknown density, but subclass monotonicity still yields a sharp lower-side comparison with the Kennedy-style bounded-density model.
added_lemmas.consumer: The corollary separates a broadly applicable privacy impossibility from the design-specific matched upper frontier.

proposed.name: Bounded-density nonprivate and private minimax risks

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declares the fuzzy-family membership lemma that the target proof uses directly to place both shared-prior supports inside the exact-uniform model.

proposed.statement: On the known exact-uniform class \(\mathcal M_H\), for \(n^{-1}\le\epsilon_n\le1\), every \(\epsilon_n\)-differentially private estimator satisfies \(R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},r_G,r_F\}=c\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\}\). The \(r_F\) branch follows by setting \(ab\asymp r_F\), \(h\asymp r_F^{1/\gamma}\), and \(\ell\asymp r_F^{1/q}\) in the component coupling before applying a central-private two-prior testing inequality.
proposed.justification: The lower bound certifies that both privacy balances are intrinsic to the causal class.
proposed.gap: Cai et al. establish the direct pointwise-regression privacy barrier, while no published result adds the coupled-nuisance \(n^2\epsilon_n\) branch for CATE.
proposed.consumer: It prevents private CATE algorithms from being benchmarked only against ordinary private regression.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Records the broader lower-bound corollary without extending the design-specific achievability or phase diagram.
proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\},\quad R_{n,\mathrm{bd}}^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c\max\{R_{n,\mathrm{bd}}^{\mathrm{NP}},\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\},\quad R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\}\ \text{if }q\ge q_0\ \text{or }\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\ge cb_n,\quad \rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}=\max\{(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)},(n^2\epsilon_n)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/(\alpha+\beta))}\}\). The bounded-density display is a lower bound only.

prose_updates.tldr: On the deliberately restricted class with a known exact-uniform covariate law and bounded observed outcomes, pointwise CATE is a regression-functional hybrid whose pure-central privacy cost has the two scales \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}=\max\{(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)},(n^2\epsilon_n)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/(\alpha+\beta))}\}\). One second-order local estimator and a positive fuzzy Hamming-transport converse yield the matched frontier whenever privacy leads or nuisance smoothness is above the nonprivate elbow. Separately, the exact-uniform class is a subclass of the aligned unknown bounded-density class because its density is one, so both privacy lower barriers also hold on that broader Kennedy-style model. This is a lower-bound transfer only: neither the occupancy-normalized estimator nor the matched phase diagram is claimed beyond exact uniformity. The remaining exact-uniform question is a stability transfer from the attained benchmark to the symbolic nonprivate minimax risk in the privacy-inactive below-elbow region.

project_justification.fill: On the known exact-uniform class, a single \(p^2+3p\)-coordinate Laplace release contains the score block, the upper-triangular Gram block, and their two exact occupancy-normalized corrections; every subsequent symmetry and spectral operation is postprocessing. Boundedness is imposed only on observed outcomes, with causal and kernel bounds derived from consistency, armwise exchangeability, and overlap. A smooth positive exact-uniform fuzzy family supplies singleton cancellation and a componentwise Hamming coupling. Because the uniform density equals one, subclass inclusion and conditional Jensen additionally transfer both privacy lower barriers, but no upper bound, to the aligned unknown bounded-density class. One open symbolic-risk transfer question remains confined to the exact-uniform model and separate from the queued nonprivate converse.

sampling_model.design: The matched estimation theorem uses a known exact-uniform covariate law \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\) with independent sampling and replacement adjacency. A separate lower-only corollary enlarges the law class to an unknown density satisfying \(L^{-1}\le dP_X/dx\le L\); the exact-uniform estimator and phase diagram are not asserted on that broader class.

prose_updates.related_work: Kennedy et al. (2024), Theorem 1 and Remark 2, analyze a bounded-density random-design Hölder model; Theorem 2 and Appendix B.8 add design-estimation conditions for attainability. Their localized fuzzy hypotheses and higher-order local R-moment architecture inform this proposal. The exact-uniform class is narrower than their design setting, while the new bounded-density corollary uses only inclusion of the uniform subclass to transfer the two privacy lower barriers; it does not transfer the exact-uniform estimator or claim Kennedy et al.'s nonprivate result settles the symbolic exact-uniform risk. Kennedy (2023), Theorems 1--3 and Sections 3--5, gives pseudo-outcome oracle inequalities and local-polynomial error bounds, but risk control alone supplies no neighboring-record stability. Niu et al. (2022), Theorem 6, proves \(f\)-DP composition for a sample-split multi-stage CATE meta-algorithm without a Hölder minimax utility theorem. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025), page 3 and Theorems 1 and 3, assume bounded observed outcomes and develop approximate-DP orthogonal two-stage CATE releases for finite or functional queries; they do not provide a pure-central Hölder pointwise minimax rate or the \(n^2\epsilon_n\) coupled-nuisance branch. Chaudhuri et al. (2024), Algorithm 1 and Theorem 2, stabilize bounded-kernel U-statistics using local Hájek projections; the exact-uniform binomial normalization here is a causal-specific construction. Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen (2024), Theorems 2.1, 3.4, and 4.4, establish pointwise Besov-regression rates under heterogeneous distributed privacy rather than one-database pure central privacy with causal nuisances. Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021), Theorems 1 and 3, and Lalanne, Garivier, and Gribonval (2023), the main transport reduction, supply private testing inequalities but no smooth causal shared-prior coupling. Nissim, Raskhodnikova, and Smith (2007), Sections 1.2--1.3, explain why typical occupancy cannot replace a worst-neighbor sensitivity certificate. Every comparator remains methodological input and informed-by positioning.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact occupancy normalization and deterministic projection geometry require a known exact-uniform random design with equal public cell volumes. Thus the upper theorem, matched frontier, and phase diagram do not extend here to an unknown or merely bounded covariate density, and the iid theorem does not automatically cover a deterministic uniform grid. Only the privacy lower barriers transfer to the broader bounded-density class, by inclusion of the uniform subclass and conditional Jensen. On the exact-uniform class, the upper theorem still contains the explicit benchmark \(b_n\); replacing it by \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\) below the nuisance elbow and outside privacy-leading regimes is the stated open-ended question, not an assumed consequence of generic output perturbation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal boundedness consequence, projection identity, pair sensitivity, fuzzy membership, component transport, upper envelope, lower envelope, and phase diagram concern the known exact-uniform class with bounded observed outcomes. The full symbolic decomposition is settled there for \(q\ge q_0\) and whenever \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\gtrsim b_n\), and it remains open for \(q<q_0\) when privacy is inactive relative to \(b_n\). The queued exact-uniform nonprivate converse is neither cited as established nor duplicated. On the aligned unknown bounded-density class, this note proves only \(R_{n,\mathrm{bd}}^{\mathrm{DP}}\gtrsim\max\{R_{n,\mathrm{bd}}^{\mathrm{NP}},r_G,r_F\}\) by conditional Jensen and subclass monotonicity; it asserts no estimator, upper rate, matched phase diagram, or symbolic transfer there. Privacy sequences with \(\epsilon_n<n^{-1}\) and deterministic fixed designs remain outside the stated theorems.
